critique.good: The six months have equal widths, making comparisons easy. Figures and headers stay intact, and most regions fit on one line. The long region wraps cleanly to two lines.
critique.problems: The long region produces one taller row, while the monthly columns have little spare room around their figures. This is nevertheless the strongest balance of the three.
critique.cause: The 135px region column allows 114px of text; each 59px month column allows exactly the stated 38px needed by the widest figures.

critique.good: Equal monthly columns provide a consistent rhythm and more breathing room for figures. Words and numbers remain intact.
critique.problems: North America and Latin America wrap, and the long region occupies three lines. The uneven row heights interrupt scanning across regions without adding useful separation.
critique.cause: Reducing the region column to 111px leaves 90px for text; the extra width goes to the six 63px month columns.

critique.good: The monthly columns are consistent and spacious, and words and figures remain intact.
critique.problems: Every region label wraps, with the long label spread over four lines. Tall rows and the narrow identifier column make the table harder to scan as a whole.
critique.cause: The 78px region column leaves only 57px for text, while each month receives 68px.

critique.good: The region labels remain recognizable, the long label wraps cleanly into two lines, and the equal month widths support comparison across rows and down columns. All figures and headers stay intact.
critique.problems: The monthly figures have very little spare horizontal space, giving the numeric columns a tight appearance.
critique.cause: Each 59px month column leaves 38px for text, exactly the stated width of the longest figures. The 133px region column leaves enough room for the long label to wrap at a space.

critique.good: The table keeps the same clear row and column rhythm, with intact figures and a clean two-line wrap for the long region label. The monthly columns have slightly more room than in r1A.
critique.problems: The region column is slightly tighter, while the extra pixel in each month column produces little visible improvement. The long region label still occupies two lines.
critique.cause: Reducing the region column to 127px makes room for six 60px month columns, each with 39px of text space.

r0A.idea: Give the region labels the most space available while keeping all six monthly values intact in equal-width columns.

r0B.idea: Balance moderate wrapping of region labels with a little more breathing room for each month.

r0C.idea: Give the monthly comparisons generous, equal space while allowing region labels to wrap across several lines without breaking words.

r1A.idea: Keep the strongest design's equal 59px monthly columns and use the remaining 133px for region labels, bringing the width within the 489px limit while aiming to preserve its clean two-line wrap.

r1B.idea: Give each month one extra pixel and test whether a 127px region column still keeps the shorter labels on one line and the long label to two lines.

understanding.purpose: Compare monthly sales across regions from January through June.
understanding.reading: Readers scan across each row to follow a region over time and down each month to compare regions.
groups: January–June are parallel monthly measures and should have consistent widths.
The region column identifies each row and needs enough space for recognizable labels.
may_wrap: Multiword region names may wrap at spaces; the long Europe, Middle East & Africa label is the main candidate.

bad.why: The narrow region column wraps three labels, while the extra width in the monthly columns does not help their short values. The resulting row heights weaken the rhythm of the table.
Every region label wraps, and the longest takes four lines. The oversized monthly columns leave broad empty spaces beside the fragmented row labels.

final.rationale: The preferred designs give the region labels most of the available flexibility while keeping all six monthly columns equal. Only the longest region label wraps, and it stays readable across two lines. The month headers and values remain intact, supporting comparison across each row.

general: Give columns that serve the same comparative role a consistent rhythm when their content needs are similar.
Allocate width where it improves reading; extra space in short numeric columns may be more useful to row labels.
Judge wrapping by its effect on row identity and scanning, rather than by line count alone.
specific: The six monthly columns each need at least 59px to contain their values with the stated padding.
A region width of 133–135px produces the same visible two-line treatment of the longest label in the preferred designs.

final.tradeoffs: r1B gives each monthly column one extra pixel at the expense of the region column; its rendering remains publishable, though the extra numeric space provides little visible benefit.
final.uncertain: A designer could reasonably consider r1B equally good because its wrapping and row heights match the preferred designs. The ranges describe the observed preferred allocations, subject to the 489px total-width limit.

A.why: The month columns have a consistent rhythm, all figures remain intact, and only the longest region label wraps.

B.why: The numbers remain intact and the rows scan well, though the first month columns feel slightly tighter than the later ones.

C.why: The figures are clear, but the narrow region column wraps three labels and makes the rows taller.

D.why: Only the longest region label wraps and the figures remain intact, though the month columns are slightly uneven.

E.why: The region column is so narrow that the header and several words break within words, making the row labels difficult to read.

reviews.unsure: A and D are very close; their small differences in column proportions are difficult to judge at this image size.

A.why: Region names remain intact, with only the long regional label wrapping; the six month columns are evenly paced and their values are easy to compare.

B.why: The row labels read cleanly, the long label wraps naturally, and the month columns have a consistent rhythm.

C.why: The numbers align clearly, but the narrow region column wraps three labels and makes the rows taller without improving comparison.

D.why: The region header and several names break within words, making row identification difficult and leaving excessive vertical space beside the figures.

E.why: Labels and values remain intact, but the month columns vary in width, giving equivalent measures a less consistent rhythm.
